## Dossier: Encounter (backend — `care`)

### FHIR R5 alignment

CARE's `Encounter` closely tracks the FHIR R5 [Encounter](https://build.fhir.org/encounter.html) resource, encoded via a Django model ([care/emr/models/encounter.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/models/encounter.py)) and Pydantic resource specs ([care/emr/resources/encounter/spec.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/resources/encounter/spec.py)).

| FHIR R5 element | CARE implementation | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | `status` field, `StatusChoices` enum | Values match FHIR's encounter-status value set exactly (using `entered_in_error` for `entered-in-error`) |
| `class` (0..*) | `encounter_class` (single value), `ClassChoices` | FHIR allows multiple classes over time; CARE stores only current + a JSON history (`encounter_class_history`), not a list |
| `priority` | `priority`, `EncounterPriorityChoices` | Maps to ActPriority-style codes |
| `subject` (Patient) | `patient` FK → `Patient` | [spec.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/resources/encounter/spec.py) L16 |
| `serviceProvider`/facility context | `facility` FK → `Facility` (PROTECT) | No direct FHIR `Organization`-as-serviceProvider field name, but conceptually equivalent |
| Encounter departments/orgs | `EncounterOrganization` join table → `FacilityOrganization` | Approximates FHIR's `Encounter.careTeam`/organization linkage; cached in `facility_organization_cache` for authz |
| `location` (backbone, 0..*, with `status`) | `FacilityLocationEncounter` model + `Encounter.current_location` cache | See Data model section |
| `participant` | `care_team` JSONField (`user_id` + `role` Coding) | Role bound to a value set (SNOMED-based), not a FHIR `Practitioner`/`PractitionerRole` resource reference |
| `appointment` | `appointment` FK → `TokenBooking` | CARE's own booking model, not FHIR `Appointment` resource directly |
| `period` (start/end) | `period` JSON (`PeriodSpec`: `start`, `end`) | [base.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/resources/base.py) L181 — both datetimes must be timezone-aware |
| `admission` (admitSource, reAdmission, dietPreference, dischargeDisposition) | `hospitalization` JSON (`HospitalizationSpec`) | Field names/semantics match FHIR R5's `Encounter.admission` backbone almost 1:1 |
| `identifier` | `external_identifier` (plain string) | No FHIR `Identifier` type/system structure, just a bare string |
| `diagnosis` | Not present on Encounter spec/model | Likely modeled via a separate `Condition` resource; link **not verified** in this pass — see Ambiguities |
| `EncounterHistory` (FHIR R5 introduced this as a separate resource for status/class history) | `status_history` / `encounter_class_history` JSON fields on the same `Encounter` row | CARE does not use a separate FHIR-style `EncounterHistory` resource — history is inlined |
| Extensions | `extensions` JSONField, validated via CARE's own `ExtensionValidator`/`ExtensionResource.encounter` plugin mechanism | [extensions/base.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/extensions/base.py) — a CARE-specific plugin extension system, not a literal FHIR `extension` element implementation |

Related linked FHIR-ish resources seen in code: `Patient` (Patient), `Facility`/`FacilityOrganization` (Organization), `FacilityLocation`/`FacilityLocationEncounter` (Location), `TokenBooking` (Appointment), `User` (Practitioner, via care team).

---

### Data model

Model: [care/emr/models/encounter.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/models/encounter.py). Spec: [care/emr/resources/encounter/spec.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/resources/encounter/spec.py).

| Attribute | Type | Required (create) | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | `StatusChoices` | Yes | — | |
| `encounter_class` | `ClassChoices` | Yes | — | |
| `priority` | `EncounterPriorityChoices` | Yes | — | |
| `period` | `PeriodSpec {start, end}` | No | `{}` | Datetimes must be tz-aware |
| `hospitalization` | `HospitalizationSpec` | No | `{}` | See below |
| `external_identifier` | `str \| None` | No | `None` | Free-text hospital reference number |
| `discharge_summary_advice` | `str \| None` | No | `None` | Cleared to `None` on update if omitted (see Business rules) |
| `patient` | UUID (create-only) | Yes | — | Resolved to `Patient` FK; excluded from update spec |
| `facility` | UUID (create-only) | Yes | — | Resolved to `Facility` FK (PROTECT) |
| `organizations` | `list[UUID]` (create-only) | No | `[]` | Deduplicated; becomes `EncounterOrganization` rows |
| `appointment` | UUID (create-only) | No | `None` | Must belong to same patient/facility; encounter can't be created if the booking already has an associated encounter |
| `care_team` | JSON (not in create/update spec — separate endpoint) | No | `{}` | Managed via `set_care_team_members` action only |
| `current_location` | FK → `FacilityLocation` | — (system-managed) | `None` | Cached pointer to the active location |
| `facility_organization_cache` | `ArrayField[int]` | — | `[]` | Cache of org IDs for authorization queries |
| `care_team_users` | `ArrayField[int]` | — | `[]` | Cache of care team user IDs for filtering/authz |
| `tags` | `ArrayField[int]` | — | `[]` | Managed via tag `set_tags`/`remove_tags` actions |
| `extensions` | JSON | — | `{}` | Plugin/extension payloads |
| `status_history` / `encounter_class_history` | JSON | — | `{}` | Append-only log of `{status, moved_at}` on every change |

**Hospitalization** ([spec.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/resources/encounter/spec.py) L44-48):

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `re_admission` | `bool \| None` | No | `None` |
| `admit_source` | `AdmitSourcesChoices \| None` | No | `None` |
| `discharge_disposition` | `DischargeDispositionChoices \| None` | No | `None` |
| `diet_preference` | `DietPreferenceChoices \| None` | No | `None` |

No backend field named "discharge date/time" exists separately — discharge timing is expected to be represented via `period.end` (unverified explicitly; see Ambiguities).

---

### Enums and coded values

All from [care/emr/resources/encounter/constants.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/resources/encounter/constants.py) unless noted.

**Status (`StatusChoices`)**: `planned`, `in_progress`, `on_hold`, `discharged`, `completed`, `cancelled`, `discontinued`, `entered_in_error`, `unknown`

- `COMPLETED_CHOICES = [completed, cancelled, entered_in_error, discontinued]` — these lock the encounter from further non-clinical edits and clinical-data submission. **`discharged` is NOT in `COMPLETED_CHOICES`** — a discharged encounter remains editable (see Suspected Code Issues).
- `ERROR_CHOICES = [entered_in_error]` — blocks writing new service requests only.
- No status state-machine/transition-graph validation exists in the backend (no "planned → in_progress → …" enforcement found anywhere in [encounter.py viewset](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/encounter.py) or [spec.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/resources/encounter/spec.py)). Any status value can be set to any other via update, as long as the current status isn't in `COMPLETED_CHOICES`.

**Encounter Class (`ClassChoices`)**: `imp`, `amb`, `obsenc`, `emer`, `vr`, `hh`

**Priority (`EncounterPriorityChoices`)**: `ASAP`, `callback_results`, `callback_for_scheduling`, `elective`, `emergency`, `preop`, `as_needed`, `routine`, `rush_reporting`, `stat`, `timing_critical`, `use_as_directed`, `urgent`

**Admit Source (`AdmitSourcesChoices`)**: `hosp_trans`, `emd`, `outp`, `born`, `gp`, `mp`, `nursing`, `psych`, `rehab`, `other` — backend display labels in [enum_display_names.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/resources/encounter/enum_display_names.py)

**Discharge Disposition (`DischargeDispositionChoices`)**: `home`, `alt_home`, `other_hcf`, `hosp`, `long`, `aadvice`, `exp`, `psy`, `rehab`, `snf`, `oth`

**Diet Preference (`DietPreferenceChoices`)**: `vegetarian`, `dairy_free`, `nut_free`, `gluten_free`, `vegan`, `halal`, `kosher`, `none`

**Re-admission**: plain boolean, not an enum.

**Location status (`LocationEncounterAvailabilityStatusChoices`, [location/spec.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/resources/location/spec.py))**: `planned`, `active`, `reserved`, `completed`
- `active` must not carry an `end_datetime` (forced to `None`).
- `completed` requires an `end_datetime`.
- Once a `FacilityLocationEncounter` reaches `completed`, its status can never change again (`"Cannot change status after marking completed"`, [location.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/location.py) L~416).

**Care team participant role**: not a fixed enum — a `Coding` bound to the `PRACTITIONER_ROLE_VALUESET` ([valueset.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/resources/encounter/valueset.py)), backed by SNOMED CT concepts under `223366009` and `224930009` ("Healthcare related organization role" / etc.). No fixed hardcoded list — it's a queryable value set.

**Tag category (`TagCategoryChoices`)**, [tag/config_spec.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/resources/tag/config_spec.py): `diet`, `drug`, `lab`, `admin`, `contact`, `clinical`, `behavioral`, `research`, `advance_directive`, `safety` (applies to all taggable resources, encounter included). `TagStatus`: `active`, `archived`.

---

### Business rules and validations

Source: [care/emr/api/viewsets/encounter.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/encounter.py), [care/emr/api/viewsets/location.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/location.py), [care/emr/api/viewsets/device.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/device.py), [care/emr/tagging/base.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/tagging/base.py).

**Creation** (`validate_data`, L127-143):
- Patient must have fewer than `MAX_ACTIVE_ENCOUNTERS_PER_PATIENT_IN_FACILITY` (default 5) non-completed encounters at that facility, else: *"Patient already has maximum number of active encounters (N) in the facility"*.
- Patient and Facility must exist (else "Patient does not exist" / "Facility does not exist").
- If an `appointment` is supplied and it already has an associated encounter: *"Encounter already has an associated booking"*.
- `status_history`/`encounter_class_history` are seeded with the initial status/class + timestamp on creation.

**Update**:
- Any status/class change appends to the respective history JSON.
- If `discharge_summary_advice` is omitted (None) on update, it is explicitly cleared.
- Encounters with status in `COMPLETED_CHOICES` (completed, cancelled, entered_in_error, discontinued) cannot be updated at all — `can_update_encounter_obj` returns `False` before checking permissions.
- On every successful update: any device with `current_encounter` pointing here is disassociated **if** the new status is in `COMPLETED_CHOICES` ([device.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/device.py) `disassociate_device_from_encounter`), and any non-completed `FacilityLocationEncounter` rows are force-closed (status → `completed`, `end_datetime` = now) and the location's `current_encounter`/`operational_status` reset ([location.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/location.py) `close_related_location_from_encounter`).
- **No backend validation requires `discharge_disposition` to be set when status becomes `discharged`.** This appears to be enforced (if at all) only on the frontend — see Suspected Code Issues.

**Restart** (`POST .../restart`):
- Only allowed if current status is in `COMPLETED_CHOICES` (so **not** allowed from `discharged`), else *"Encounter is not in a completed state"*.
- Blocked if `modified_date` is older than `ENCOUNTER_RESTART_TIME_LIMIT_HOURS` (default **0**) hours ago: *"Encounter cannot be restarted after N hours"*. With the default of 0 hours, this check effectively always fails (see Suspected Code Issues).
- On success: status is forced to `in_progress` (bypassing normal update pathway/history append logic).

**Location association** (`FacilityLocationEncounterViewSet`, [location.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/location.py)):
- Cannot assign an encounter to a location whose `mode` is `kind` (only `instance`-mode locations, e.g., actual beds, not location categories): *"Cannot assign encounters to location kind"*.
- `end_datetime` must be ≥ `start_datetime`: *"End Datetime should be greater than Start Datetime"*.
- `completed` status requires an `end_datetime`: *"End Datetime is required for completed status"*.
- Overlapping schedule conflict check: a new/updated assignment with an `end_datetime` cannot overlap another `active`/`planned` assignment at the same location: *"Conflict in schedule"*.
- Only one location assignment can be `active` at a time system-wide per location; `reset_encounter_location_association` recomputes `Encounter.current_location` and the location's availability/operational status whenever assignments change — the location becomes `reserved` (system availability) if there's an active encounter, else `available`.
- Once a location-encounter row is `completed`, its status is immutable.
- Both the target location and the encounter must belong to the same facility ("Encounter Incompatible with Location").

**Care team** (`set_care_team_members`):
- Rejects duplicate `user_id`s in the same request ("repeats are not allowed").
- Each member must have view access to the encounter (odd self-check — see Suspected Code Issues).
- Entire care team list is replaced wholesale on each call (not additive).

**Organizations/departments** (`organizations_add`/`organizations_remove`):
- Organization must belong to the same facility as the encounter ("Organization Incompatible with Encounter").
- Cannot add a duplicate organization ("Organization already exists") or remove one not present ("Organization does not exist").

**Tags** (`SingleFacilityTagManager.set_tag`, [tagging/base.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/tagging/base.py)):
- Requires `can_apply_tag_config` authorization per tag.
- Cannot apply the same tag twice ("Tag already set").
- Tag's configured `resource` must equal `encounter` ("Tag resource does not match resource type").
- If the tag has a `root_tag_config` (i.e., belongs to a mutually-exclusive tag family/parent), only one tag from that family can be applied at a time ("Tag Parent is already set").

**Facility identifier** (`set_facility_idenitifier` action) — manages `PatientIdentifier`/`PatientIdentifierConfig` records (a facility-level MRN/identifier system), not the encounter's own `external_identifier` field. Auto-maintained identifier configs cannot be manually edited.

---

### Permissions — full RBAC trace

Definitions: [care/security/permissions/encounter.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/security/permissions/encounter.py). `CLINICAL_DATA_ACCESS_ROLES = [ADMIN_ROLE, DOCTOR_ROLE, NURSE_ROLE, FACILITY_ADMIN_ROLE]` ([role.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/security/roles/role.py)).

| Operation | viewset hook | AuthorizationController slug | Handler ([authorization/encounter.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/security/authorization/encounter.py)) | Human-readable permission name | Roles |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Create encounter | `authorize_create` | `can_create_encounter_obj` | `can_create_encounter_obj` → `EncounterPermissions.can_create_encounter` | **"Can Create encounter"** | Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Facility Admin |
| Retrieve/read encounter | `authorize_retrieve` | `can_view_patient_obj` OR `can_view_encounter_obj` | `can_view_encounter_obj` → `EncounterPermissions.can_read_encounter` | **"Can Read encounter"** | Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Facility Admin |
| List encounters | `get_queryset` (facility filter) | `get_filtered_encounters` | uses `EncounterPermissions.can_list_encounter` | **"Can list encounters"** | Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Facility Admin |
| Update (non-clinical: status, class, priority, hospitalization, identifiers, discharge advice) | `authorize_update` | `can_update_encounter_obj` | blocks if completed, else `EncounterPermissions.can_write_encounter` | **"Update Encounter non clinical"** | Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Facility Admin |
| Restart (completed → in_progress) | custom action | `can_restart_encounter_obj` | requires status in `COMPLETED_CHOICES`, then `EncounterPermissions.can_write_encounter` | **"Update Encounter non clinical"** | Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Facility Admin |
| Manage organizations (add/remove) | `authorize_update` (reused) | `can_update_encounter_obj` | same as Update | **"Update Encounter non clinical"** | Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Facility Admin |
| Manage care team | `authorize_update` (reused) + per-member `can_view_encounter_obj` | `can_update_encounter_obj` | same as Update | **"Update Encounter non clinical"** | Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Facility Admin |
| Manage tags | `authorize_set_tags`/`authorize_remove_tags` → `authorize_update` | `can_update_encounter_obj` (+ per-tag `can_apply_tag_config`) | same as Update | **"Update Encounter non clinical"** | Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Facility Admin |
| Manage location (assign) | `FacilityLocationEncounterViewSet.authorize_create/update` | `can_update_encounter_obj` + `can_list_facility_location_obj` | same as Update, plus location authz | **"Update Encounter non clinical"** (+ location permission, not traced here) | Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Facility Admin |
| Set facility identifier | `authorize_update` (reused) | `can_update_encounter_obj` | same as Update | **"Update Encounter non clinical"** | Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Facility Admin |
| Read encounter-related clinical data (Observations, Medicines, etc.) | (used elsewhere, e.g. observation/medication viewsets) | `can_view_encounter_clinical_data` | `EncounterPermissions.can_read_encounter_clinical_data` | **"Can Read encounter related clinical data"** | Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Facility Admin |
| Write encounter-related clinical data | (used elsewhere) | `can_update_encounter_clinical_data` | blocks if completed, else `EncounterPermissions.can_write_encounter_clinical_data` | **"Update Encounter related clinical data"** | Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Facility Admin |
| Submit questionnaire on encounter | (questionnaire viewset) | `can_submit_encounter_questionnaire_obj` | blocks if completed, else `EncounterPermissions.can_submit_encounter_questionnaire` | **"Can submit questionnaire about patient encounters"** | Staff, Doctor, Nurse, Admin, Facility Admin |

Role determination is context-sensitive: `find_roles_on_encounter` derives applicable roles from the user's `FacilityOrganizationUser` membership across **both** the encounter's associated organizations (`facility_organization_cache`) **and** its current location's organization cache — i.e., a user can gain encounter access purely through being assigned to the department that owns the patient's current bed/location, not just the encounter's own departments.

---

### Configuration flags

Source: [config/settings/config.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/config/settings/config.py).

| Flag | Effect | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `MAX_ACTIVE_ENCOUNTERS_PER_PATIENT_IN_FACILITY` | Max concurrent non-completed encounters a patient can have at one facility; creation blocked beyond this | 5 |
| `ENCOUNTER_RESTART_TIME_LIMIT_HOURS` | Hours after last modification within which a completed encounter can be restarted | 0 (effectively disables restart unless raised — see below) |

No `plug_config.py` hooks specific to Encounter were found in this pass (not exhaustively verified).

---

### API-level flows

1. **Create an encounter** — `POST` create (patient, facility, class, status, priority, optional organizations/appointment).
2. **View/retrieve an encounter** — `GET` detail (includes care team, organizations, location history, tags, permissions).
3. **List encounters** — `GET` list, filterable by facility, status, class, priority, external identifier, phone/name, location, date range, live/closed, organization, care-team user.
4. **Update encounter** (status, class, priority, period, hospitalization details, external identifier, discharge advice) — `PATCH`/`PUT`.
5. **Restart a completed encounter** — `POST .../restart`.
6. **Manage organizations/departments** — `GET .../organizations`, `POST .../organizations_add`, `DELETE .../organizations_remove`.
7. **Manage care team** — `POST .../set_care_team_members` (full replace).
8. **Set facility/patient identifier for the encounter's patient** — `POST .../set_facility_idenitifier`.
9. **Manage tags** — `POST .../set_tags`, `POST .../remove_tags`.
10. **Associate/manage encounter location** — via `FacilityLocationEncounterViewSet` (create/update/destroy of location-encounter assignment), plus a `FacilityLocationViewSet.associate_encounter` action stub.

---

### SUSPECTED CODE ISSUES

1. **`discharged` is excluded from `COMPLETED_CHOICES`** ([constants.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/resources/encounter/constants.py)) — a discharged encounter remains fully editable (status can be changed again, devices/locations are not auto-closed via that path), unlike `completed`/`cancelled`/`discontinued`/`entered_in_error`. This seems inconsistent with the intent (discharge should probably be terminal) and contradicts the old docs' implication that discharge closes the encounter.
2. **`ENCOUNTER_RESTART_TIME_LIMIT_HOURS` defaults to 0** ([config.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/config/settings/config.py) L254-256) — combined with the strict `<` comparison in [encounter.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/encounter.py) restart action, this makes restart fail unconditionally for any deployment that doesn't override the env var, since `modified_date` will (almost) always be earlier than `care_now()`.
3. **No backend requirement that `discharge_disposition` be set when status transitions to `discharged`** — contradicts the old doc's claim ("You must select a Discharge Disposition when you set the status to Discharged"). If this is enforced, it must be purely a frontend/zod rule; not present in `EncounterUpdateSpec` or any validator in [spec.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/resources/encounter/spec.py).
4. **No status transition state machine** at all — any status can move to any other status via a normal update, as long as the encounter is not already in `COMPLETED_CHOICES`. There's no protection against, e.g., going from `planned` directly to `discharged`.
5. **`set_care_team_members` self-check is odd** ([encounter.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/encounter.py) L~415): for each member being added, it re-checks `can_view_encounter_obj(request.user, encounter)` — i.e., it checks the *requesting user's* view permission repeatedly per loop iteration (a no-op since it's the same check every time), not the *added member's* permission. The error message ("Treating doctor does not have permission on encounter") suggests the intent was likely to validate the member being added, not the requester redundantly.
6. **`FacilityLocationViewSet.associate_encounter` action is a stub** — ends with `# TODO, Association models yet to be built` and performs authorization checks but no actual persistence ([location.py](file:///Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/location.py) L~562). Likely dead/incomplete code; the real location-assignment path is `FacilityLocationEncounterViewSet`.
7. **Inconsistent casing in `EncounterPriorityChoices`** — `ASAP` is uppercase while all sibling values (`stat`, `elective`, `routine`, etc.) are lowercase. Likely accidental.
8. **`set_facility_idenitifier`** action name has a typo ("idenitifier") baked into the URL/action name.

---

### AMBIGUITIES / UNVERIFIED

1. Whether `Condition` (diagnosis) resources link to `Encounter` was **not verified** in this pass — FHIR's `Encounter.diagnosis` element has no obvious counterpart on the `Encounter` model/spec.
2. Whether "Discharge Date and Time" (mentioned in the old docs) maps to `period.end`, or is a separate untracked field, is **not verified** — no explicit discharge-date field exists on `HospitalizationSpec` or `Encounter`.
3. Frontend-side enforcement of "discharge disposition required on discharge" was **not checked** (out of scope for this backend-only pass) — flagging for the frontend researcher to confirm/deny.
4. The exact permission slug gating `can_list_facility_location_obj` (used when assigning locations) was **not traced** in this pass — only confirmed it exists and gates location-related encounter actions.
5. Whether any `plug_config.py` plugins alter Encounter behavior was **not exhaustively checked** — only core `config/settings/config.py` flags were verified.
6. The relationship between `external_identifier` (encounter's own field) and the `PatientIdentifierConfig`/`set_facility_idenitifier` system is unclear — they appear to be two separate identifier mechanisms, but this was not fully confirmed to be intentional versus a naming/documentation confusion in the old docs (which conflate them into a single "Hospital Identifier" concept).
7. Old docs list a "Hospital Identifier" component in Key Attributes — likely maps to `external_identifier`, but this label wasn't found verbatim in backend code (labels are frontend/i18n concerns, out of scope here).

All source facts gathered. Here is the dossier.

## Dossier: Encounter (frontend, `care_fe`)

### 1. Entry points and navigation

**A. Facility sidebar → Patients → encounter lists**
- Nav group `Patients` (`t("patients")`) in the facility sidebar → children (source: [facility-nav.tsx](care_fe/src/components/ui/sidebar/facility/facility-nav.tsx#L60-L86)):
  - "Search Patients" → `/facility/:facilityId/patients`
  - "All Encounters" (`t("all_encounters")`, only shown if more than one encounter class is configured) → `/facility/:facilityId/encounters/patients/all`
  - One item per configured encounter class, label `t("encounter_class_encounters", { encounterClassName: t("encounter_class__<class>") })` → `/facility/:facilityId/encounters/patients/:encounterClass`
  - "Locations" (`t("locations")`) → `/facility/:facilityId/encounters/locations`
- Routes resolve to `EncountersOverview` ([EncountersOverview.tsx](care_fe/src/pages/Encounters/EncountersOverview.tsx)) with a `patients`/`locations` tab, defined in [PatientRoutes.tsx](care_fe/src/Routers/routes/PatientRoutes.tsx#L18-L56).

**B. From the Facility patient search → PatientHome**
1. Sidebar "Patients" → "Search Patients" → `PatientIndex` ([PatientIndex.tsx](care_fe/src/components/Patient/PatientIndex.tsx)).
2. Search by identifier or search by encounter (name/external identifier) — tab switch via `SEARCH_MODE_IDENTIFIER` / `SEARCH_MODE_ENCOUNTER`.
3. Selecting a patient (or verifying with year-of-birth for partial matches) navigates to `/facility/:facilityId/patients/home` → `PatientHome` ([PatientHome.tsx](care_fe/src/pages/Patient/PatientHome.tsx)).
4. On `PatientHome`, quick action **"Create Encounter"** (`t("create_encounter")`, only if `canCreateEncounter`) opens the `CreateEncounterForm` sheet.

**C. From the Patient page (facility-scoped) → Encounters tab**
- Patient page tab "Encounters" (`t("encounters")`, route `encounters`) → `EncounterHistory` ([EncounterHistory.tsx](care_fe/src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/EncounterHistory.tsx)), listed in [PatientDetailsTab/index.tsx](care_fe/src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/index.tsx#L33-L45).
- Empty state shows **"Create Encounter"** button (only when `facilityId` is present).

**D. From an Appointment**
- Appointment detail page → "Quick Actions" panel ([AppointmentDetail.tsx](care_fe/src/pages/Appointments/AppointmentDetail.tsx#L466-L525)):
  - If a booked/checked-in appointment has **no** associated encounter: **"Start Consultation"** (`t("start_consultation")`) opens `CreateEncounterForm` with `defaultStatus=IN_PROGRESS` and links the appointment; on success the appointment status is set to `in_consultation`.
  - If the appointment already has an associated encounter: **"Start Consultation"** just updates appointment status and navigates to the encounter's Overview tab.
  - **"Create Planned Encounter"** (`t("create_planned_encounter")`) — also shown when there is no associated encounter, opens `CreateEncounterForm` with default `PLANNED` status, linked to the appointment.

**E. Home tab on `PatientHome`**
- `PatientHomeEncounters` ([PatientHomeEncounters.tsx](care_fe/src/pages/Patient/home/PatientHomeEncounters.tsx)) shows tabs "Active" (`t("active")`) / "Completed" (`t("completed")`) encounter lists for the patient at that facility.

**Encounter show/overview route**
- `/facility/:facilityId/patient/:patientId/encounter/:encounterId/:tab` and `/organization/:organizationId/patient/:patientId/encounter/:encounterId/:tab` → `EncounterShow` wrapped in `EncounterProvider` ([ConsultationRoutes.tsx](care_fe/src/Routers/routes/ConsultationRoutes.tsx#L119-L131)).

---

### 2. Screens and layout

**Create Encounter form** (Sheet, [CreateEncounterForm.tsx](care_fe/src/components/Encounter/CreateEncounterForm.tsx)) — title "Initiate Patient Encounter" (`t("initiate_encounter")`), description "Begin a new clinical encounter for **{{patientName}}**…" (`begin_clinical_encounter`):

| Field | Label | Required | Input type | Options/notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| start_date | "Date and Time" (`date_and_time`) | Yes (schema field, always present) | Date picker + time input | Disabled to future dates unless status is Planned |
| encounter_class | "Type of Encounter" (`type_of_encounter`) | Yes | Icon-button grid | Options = `careConfig.encounterClasses` (subset of the 6 classes), each with `encounter_class__<v>` label and `encounter_class_description__<v>` description |
| status | "Status" (`status`) | Yes | Select | Only `in_progress`, `planned`, `on_hold` selectable at creation |
| priority | "Priority" (no i18n key used — hardcoded literal "Priority" string, see Suspected Issues) | Yes | Select | All `ENCOUNTER_PRIORITY` values, default `routine` |
| tags | "Tags" (`t("tags", {count:2})`) | No | Tag popover selector (`TagSelectorPopover`, resource=`encounter`) | Multi-select of facility tag configs |
| organizations | (no visible `FormLabel`, rendered by `FacilityOrganizationSelector`) | Yes (`min(1)`, error "At least one department is required") | Department/organization multi-select | Favorite list `encounter_departments` |

Submit button disabled while `organizations` is empty or pending. Buttons: "Cancel" (`cancel`) / "Create Encounter" (`create_encounter`, shows "Creating…"/`creating` while pending).

**Encounter Show page** ([EncounterShow.tsx](care_fe/src/pages/Encounters/EncounterShow.tsx)):
- Patient header + deceased banner.
- Optional `AppointmentEncounterHeader` strip if the primary encounter has a linked appointment/token.
- Encounter summary line: class label, facility name (if viewing non-primary encounter), current location (icon + name from `location_form__<form>`), start–end dates ("Ongoing" if open), and status Badge (`encounter_status__<status>`).
- Left rail: `EncounterHistorySelector` — a switcher between multiple encounters for the same patient, with filters (status, department, care team, date, tags) using `MultiFilter`.
- "Encounter Actions" button opens `EncounterCommandDialog` (a searchable command palette of all actions/navigation, see Flows).
- Tabs (`NavTabs`, labels from `ENCOUNTER_TAB__<key>`): Overview ("Overview"/`updates`), Plots, Observations, Medicines, Responses ("Responses"), Service Requests, Diagnostic Reports, Files, Notes, Devices, Consents, plus any plugin tabs. All except Overview/Devices/Consents require `canReadClinicalData`.

**Overview tab side panel** (`SummaryPanelActionsTab`, [summary-panel-actions.tab.tsx](care_fe/src/pages/Encounters/tabs/overview/summary-panel-actions.tab.tsx)) — buttons: "Manage Consents", "Manage Care Team", "Update Location", "Update Department", "Dispense", and a bottom "Mark for discharge"/"Mark as Completed" button (label depends on `encounterRequiresDischarge`). On small screens it also renders inline detail widgets: Account, Encounter Tags, Locations, Manage Care Team, Departments and Teams, Hospitalization Details, Discharge Details.

**Update Encounter Details / Discharge form** (rendered as an "encounter" questionnaire, [EncounterQuestion.tsx](care_fe/src/components/Questionnaire/QuestionTypes/EncounterQuestion.tsx)):

| Field | Label | Required | Input type | Options |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| status | "Encounter Status" (`encounter_status`) | Yes | Select | Disabled once Discharged; list excludes Discharged/Unknown unless already discharged |
| encounter_class | "Encounter Class" (`encounter_class`) | Yes | Select | `careConfig.encounterClasses` |
| priority | "Priority" (`priority`) | Yes | Select | All `ENCOUNTER_PRIORITY` |
| external_identifier | "Hospital Identifier" (`hospital_identifier`) | No | Text input | placeholder "IP/OP/OBS/EMR Number" |
| (button) | "Discharge Patient" / "Mark for discharge" (`discharge_patient` / `mark_for_discharge`) | — | Button | Shown only if not yet discharged; sets status to Discharged |
| discharge_summary_advice | "Discharge Summary Advice" (`discharge_summary_advice`) | No | Textarea | Shown once discharged or already has a value |
| **Hospitalization Details** section — shown only for encounter_class in `imp`, `obsenc`, `emer` | "Hospitalization Details" (`hospitalization_details`) | — | — | — |
| hospitalization.re_admission | "Re-admission" (`readmission`) | No | Switch | boolean |
| hospitalization.admit_source | "Admit Source" (`admit_source`) | No | Select | `ENCOUNTER_ADMIT_SOURCE` |
| hospitalization.discharge_disposition | "Discharge Disposition" (`discharge_disposition`, marked with `*`) | **Yes when status=Discharged and class ∈ {imp, obsenc, emer}** | Select | `ENCOUNTER_DISCHARGE_DISPOSITION` |
| period.end | "Discharge Date and Time" (`discharge_date_time`) | No (shown only when status=Discharged) | Date + time picker | Cannot be before `period.start` |
| hospitalization.diet_preference | "Diet Preference" (`diet_preference`) | No | Select | `ENCOUNTER_DIET_PREFERENCE` |

**Location Sheet** ([LocationSheet.tsx](care_fe/src/components/Location/LocationSheet.tsx)) — two tabs: "Assign" and "History" (`LocationHistory` component). Assign tab lets you browse/select a bed/location, choose planned/reserved/active status and start/end time, move the patient (optionally keeping the old bed reserved), or complete/cancel a bed stay. If the target bed's current occupant encounter is already `discharged`, a confirm dialog is shown before proceeding; otherwise an "occupied" dialog blocks the action.

**Care Team Sheet** ([CareTeamSheet.tsx](care_fe/src/components/CareTeam/CareTeamSheet.tsx)) — title "Manage Care Team" or "View Care Team" (`manage_care_team` / `view_care_team`, depending on `canWrite`). Fields to add a member: Facility Organization selector (department), `UserSelector` (scoped by chosen department), and a role selector (`ValueSetSelect`, FHIR value-set driven `Code`, not a static enum with i18n labels). Members list supports "Make Primary" and remove (with confirm dialog).

**Link Departments Sheet** ([LinkDepartmentsSheet.tsx](care_fe/src/components/Patient/LinkDepartmentsSheet.tsx)) — a Facility Organization multi-selector plus a list of currently linked organizations, each removable via a trash icon (with per-item pending spinner).

**Encounter Tags panel** ([encounter-tags.tsx](care_fe/src/pages/Encounters/tabs/overview/summary-panel-details-tab/encounter-tags.tsx)) — "Encounter Tags" (`encounter_tags`) header with edit icon opening `TagAssignmentSheet` (entity type `encounter`), only visible/editable when `canWriteSelectedEncounter`.

---

### 4. User flows

**1. Create an Encounter**
- Entry points: PatientHome quick action, Patient "Encounters" tab empty state, Appointment quick actions ("Start Consultation" / "Create Planned Encounter").
- Steps: open `CreateEncounterForm` sheet → fill Date/Time, Type of Encounter, Status, Priority, Tags, Departments (required) → "Create Encounter".
- Success toast: "Encounter created successfully" (`encounter_created`). Redirects to the encounter's Overview tab unless `disableRedirectOnSuccess` (dispense flow redirects elsewhere instead).
- Validation error toast/inline message: "Future date is only allowed for planned encounters" (`encounter_future_date_restriction`) if a non-planned status has a future start date; "At least one department is required" if no organization selected.

**2. Start / Admit (from an Appointment)**
- If no encounter exists yet on a booked/checked-in appointment: "Start Consultation" opens the create-encounter sheet pre-set to `IN_PROGRESS`; on success the appointment is updated to `in_consultation` status.
- If encounter already exists: "Start Consultation" updates the appointment to `in_consultation` and navigates straight to the encounter Overview tab. No confirmation dialog.

**3. Update Encounter Details**
- Entry: Encounter Actions command palette → "Update Encounter Details" (`update_encounter_details`), shortcut `Shift+U`; or shortcut `shift+u` directly while on an encounter page.
- Opens the "encounter" questionnaire form (fields listed in section 2) at `.../questionnaire/encounter`.
- Submitting persists via the questionnaire submit flow (batch API); no distinct toast text was found specific to this form beyond the generic questionnaire submission flow (not verified — see Ambiguities).

**4. Complete / Mark as complete**
- Entry: Command palette "Mark as Completed"/"Mark for discharge" (label depends on `encounterRequiresDischarge`), or the Overview side-panel button, or via keyboard shortcut `m c`.
- If the encounter is Inpatient (`imp`) and not yet discharged, `encounterRequiresDischarge` redirects the user to the Update Encounter Details form with `?toDischarge=true` (forces status to Discharged) instead of showing the completion dialog.
- Otherwise, shows `MarkEncounterAsCompletedDialog` — title "Mark as complete", body "Are you sure you would like to mark this encounter as complete?" (`mark_encounter_as_complete_confirmation`), with an extra warning banner ("mark_everything_as_complete_description") if invoked as "mark everything" (`completeEverything`, only reachable via `actions.markAsCompleted(true)` from the command dialog's "mark-as-complete" id).
- Confirm → batch request closes the encounter (status→Completed, period.end set) and, if linked, closes the appointment (status→Fulfilled) and token (status→Fulfilled).
- Success toasts: "Encounter Completed" (`encounter_marked_as_complete`) and, if an appointment was closed, "Appointment closed successfully" (`appointment_closed_successfully`).

**5. Discharge an Encounter**
- Reached via the "Mark for discharge" path above for Inpatient/Observation/Emergency classes, or directly by setting Status=Discharged in Update Encounter Details.

Both dossiers are in and cross-resolve several of each other's gaps. Here is the merged picture for your confirmation before any writing starts.

## Proposed flow list (in the order a user meets them)

| # | Flow | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Create an Encounter | The "Initiate Patient Encounter" sheet, from all three entry points: the patient page quick action (shortcut `e`), the patient's Encounters tab empty state, and an appointment's **Start Consultation** / **Create Planned Encounter** (shortcuts `1` and `2`) |
| 2 | Update Encounter details | The encounter questionnaire form (`Shift+U`): status, class, priority, Hospital Identifier, and the Hospitalization Details section |
| 3 | Assign or move the Encounter location | Location sheet Assign tab (shortcut `l`), moving a patient between beds, keeping the old bed reserved, occupied-bed dialogs, History tab |
| 4 | Manage the Encounter care team | Add member by department + user + role, Make Primary, remove with confirmation |
| 5 | Manage Encounter departments | Link Departments sheet, add and remove organizations |
| 6 | Manage Encounter tags | Tag panel on the Overview tab (the only entry point — it is not in the command palette) |
| 7 | Discharge a Patient | Mark for discharge → status Discharged, mandatory Discharge Disposition, Discharge Date and Time, Discharge Summary Advice |
| 8 | Complete an Encounter | Mark as complete dialog (`m c`), the batch close of the linked appointment and token |
| 9 | Restart an Encounter | Restart Encounter action from the command palette |

**Changes from the existing docs:** the old `start_an_encounter.md` disappears — the research shows "Start Consultation" is not a separate operation. It either opens the same create form pre-set to In Progress, or, when an encounter already exists, only moves the appointment to In Consultation and navigates to the encounter. I propose folding it into flow 1. Say the word if you want it kept separate.

**Optional extra flow** not in the old set: *Find and open an Encounter* (the facility sidebar encounter lists per class, the All Encounters list, patient search by identifier or by encounter, and the encounter history selector with its filters). Tell me whether to include it.

## Key attributes and their display labels

**Status:** Planned, In Progress, On Hold, Discharged, Completed, Cancelled, Discontinued, Entered in error, Unknown.
**Class:** Inpatient, Ambulatory, Observation, Emergency, Virtual, Home Health — restricted per deployment by configuration.
**Priority:** Stat, ASAP, Emergency, Urgent, Routine, Elective, Rush reporting, Timing critical, Callback results, Callback for scheduling, Pre-op, As needed, Use as directed.
**Admit Source:** Transferred from other hospital, From accident/emergency department, From outpatient department, Born in hospital, General Practitioner referral, Medical Practitioner/physician referral, From nursing home, From psychiatric hospital, From rehabilitation facility, Other.
**Discharge Disposition:** Home, Alternate home, Other health care facility, Hospice, Long term care, Left against advice, Expired, Psychiatric hospital, Rehabilitation, Skilled nursing facility, Other.
**Diet Preference:** Vegetarian, Dairy free, Nut free, Gluten free, Vegan, Halal, Kosher, None.
**Other fields:** Hospital Identifier, Re-admission, Discharge Date and Time, Discharge Summary Advice, Tags, Departments, Care team, Current location.
**Permissions (backend human-readable names):** "Can Create encounter", "Can Read encounter", "Can list encounters", "Update Encounter non clinical", "Can Read encounter related clinical data", "Update Encounter related clinical data", "Can submit questionnaire about patient encounters". Held by Admin, Doctor, Nurse and Facility Admin.

## Ambiguities — I need your decision on these

1. **Discharged is not a terminal state.** Neither repository treats it as one: the backend excludes it from its completed set, and the frontend keeps a discharged encounter writable. So after discharge, a user can still change the status, move the location and edit the care team. The old docs implied discharge closes the encounter. **Do I document the real behavior, or is this a bug you want fixed first?**
2. **Restart is contradictory across the two repos.** The backend allows a restart from Completed, Cancelled, Discontinued and Entered in error, but its time-limit setting defaults to **0 hours**, which makes every restart fail on a default deployment. The frontend shows the action only for Completed and applies no time check at all. **Do I document restart as "available for completed encounters, subject to a deployment time limit", or drop the flow until this is settled?**
3. **Location assignment statuses (Planned, Active, Reserved, Completed) have no translation keys.** The frontend researcher could not confirm what text the user actually sees. I will not guess. Can you confirm the labels, or should I have a researcher re-verify by reading the rendered component?
4. **Care team role labels come from a FHIR value set at runtime**, not from a fixed list, so I can only describe the role picker generically, without naming the roles. Confirm that is acceptable.
5. **The submit confirmation text for Update Encounter details** was not traced — it goes through the generic questionnaire pipeline. I will omit any toast text for that flow unless you want it verified.
6. **Old files.** The existing folder holds ten `snake_case` flow files. The new naming is `1. Create an Encounter.md`. I have no delete tool, so the old files will remain alongside the new ones unless you remove them or authorize the reviewer to do it.

## Code issues logged (no action taken)

- `care_fe`: the Priority field label on the create form is a hardcoded English string, not translated.
- `care_fe`: diet preference label reads "Diary free" instead of "Dairy free".
- `care_fe`: stray `encounter_class__completed`, `encounter_class__in_progress`, `encounter_class__planned` translation keys that duplicate status values; a dead lowercase `encounter_priority__asap` key; duplicate `readmission` / `re_admission` keys with different casing.
- `care_fe`: Restart Encounter fires immediately with no confirmation dialog, unlike Mark as complete.
- `care`: the restart time limit defaults to 0 hours, which blocks all restarts.
- `care`: the care team member check re-validates the requesting user instead of the member being added.
- `care`: no status transition rules at all — any status can jump to any other.
- `care`: a stub `associate_encounter` action and a typo in the `set_facility_idenitifier` action name.

Confirm the flow list and answer the six points, and I will dispatch the writers.

Now I'm preparing writer briefs for each document. I'll create a shared facts block covering FHIR alignment, key attributes, enums, statuses, permissions, and relationships, then customize each brief with flow-specific details and cross-links to sibling documents.

For Flow 1, I'm documenting the entry points: the Patient page quick action with keyboard shortcut, the Encounters tab empty state, and the Appointment detail page options to either start a consultation (moving the appointment to In Consultation status) or create a planned encounter. The form itself is titled "Initiate Patient Encounter" with a description that includes the patient's name.

The form requires Date and Time (with future dates only allowed for Planned status), Type of Encounter selected from an icon grid based on deployment config, Status limited to In Progress/Planned/On Hold, Priority defaulting to Routine, optional Tags, and at least one Department. I'm also noting that deployment configuration controls which encounter types are available.

For updating encounters, I'm looking at a separate flow accessed via the command palette with keyboard shortcuts, where users can modify Status (disabled once Discharged), Class, Priority, and optional Hospital Identifier. Inpatient, Observation, and Emergency encounters show additional hospitalization details like re-admission status, admit source, discharge disposition, and diet preference. The update goes through standard questionnaire submission, and there's a separate discharge action covered elsewhere. The permission required is "Update Encounter non clinical".

For assigning encounter locations, there's a dedicated flow accessed through the command palette or the Overview panel that opens a location sheet with Assign and History tabs—users browse and select a bed or location, set the status (Planned, Reserved, or Active), and specify start and end times.

Only actual beds or rooms can hold an encounter, not location categories. When moving an encounter, you can optionally keep the previous bed reserved or complete it to free it up. If the target bed's occupant is already discharged, a confirmation dialog appears; if it's occupied by an active encounter, a blocking dialog prevents the move with no override option.

Stays have strict rules: end time must be on or after start time, completed stays require an end time and can't be modified afterward, and overlapping stays at the same location are rejected with a conflict message. Each patient can only have one active location at a time, which displays as Reserved while occupied and Available once freed. The history tab shows past stays.

In the stays list, each entry shows edit, complete, and cancel options with confirmation dialogs. When an encounter closes—whether completed, cancelled, discontinued, or marked as entered in error—any open location stay automatically closes as well. Location types have specific display names like Site, Building, Wing, Ward, Level, Corridor, Room, Bed, Vehicle, House, Cabinet, Road, Area, and Jurisdiction.

Removing a member requires confirmation while promoting someone to primary just moves them to the top. The backend replaces the entire care team list on save and rejects duplicates, and membership can grant access to the encounter itself.

For departments, I'm handling a separate flow where users link multiple departments to the encounter through a multi-select sheet, with validation rules that check facility compatibility, prevent duplicate additions, and confirm removals. Departments are set at creation with at least one required, and they control visibility of the encounter.

Now for tags, the entry point is the Encounter Tags panel in the Overview tab with an edit icon—not accessible through the command palette. The tag assignment sheet is scoped to encounters and enforces several rules: tags must be configured for encounters, can't be applied twice, and when part of a mutually exclusive family, only one from that family applies. Tags can also be set during encounter creation, and they span categories like Diet, Drug, Lab, Admin, Contact, Clinical, Behavioral, Research, Advance Directive, and Safety.

For discharging a patient, I can trigger it from the Overview side panel's "Mark for discharge" button, the command palette, or by setting Status to Discharged directly in the Update Encounter Details form. For inpatient encounters, "Mark as Completed" redirects to that form with discharge pre-selected. Discharge Disposition becomes required for inpatient, observation, and emergency encounters when discharged, and the Discharge Date and Time field appears but can't be set before the encounter start. Once discharged, a Discharge Summary Advice section displays, and deployments can pre-fill a default discharge disposition.

After discharge, the status field is disabled in the form, but the encounter stays open and editable—I can still modify location, care team, departments, and tags, and I need to mark it complete to actually close it. This requires the "Update Encounter non clinical" permission.

To complete an encounter, I use the command palette or the Overview side panel button. If it's an inpatient encounter that hasn't been discharged yet, the system routes me to discharge first. Otherwise, a "Mark as complete" dialog appears.

On confirmation, the encounter status changes to Completed with an end time set, any linked appointment and token move to Fulfilled, and I see toasts confirming the encounter and appointment closure. After completion, open location stays close automatically, devices release, and the encounter becomes read-only with no new clinical data allowed.

Restarting an encounter is accessible through the command palette with no shortcut or confirmation dialog—it executes immediately. The action only appears when the encounter is Completed, I'm working within the facility, and viewing the encounter itself. It sets the status back to In Progress and shows a success toast, though there's a deployment-configured time window (defaulting to zero hours) within which a completed encounter can be restarted; exceeding that window triggers a failure message. Both actions require the "Update Encounter non clinical" permission.

Now I'm organizing the documentation structure and preparing to write the briefs, including assembling the sibling document links that will be shared across each flow document.

### FHIR R5 alignment
Care's Encounter follows the FHIR R5 Encounter resource (https://build.fhir.org/encounter.html). Link it on first mention.
Care implements: status, class, priority, subject (the patient), the facility that provides the service, location, participant (as the care team), appointment, period (start and end), and the admission details (admit source, re-admission, diet preference, discharge disposition). Care records one encounter class at a time and keeps a history of every status change and class change on the encounter itself, instead of a separate FHIR EncounterHistory resource. Care stores a single free-text hospital identifier rather than the structured FHIR identifier. Care's Encounter has no diagnosis element.
Related resources an Encounter links to: Patient, Organization (the facility and its departments), Location (the bed or room), and Appointment (the booking the encounter started from).

### What an Encounter is, for the reader
An Encounter records one interaction between a patient and the facility — an outpatient visit, an admission, an observation stay, an emergency visit, a virtual consultation, or a home visit. It groups everything the care team records for that interaction. A patient can have several encounters at a facility at the same time; the deployment sets the maximum (5 unless the deployment changes it).

### Key attributes (use these user-facing labels)
- Status
- Type of Encounter (called Encounter Class on the update form)
- Priority
- Date and Time (the start), and Discharge Date and Time (the end)
- Hospital Identifier — a free-text reference number the facility uses, such as an IP, OP, OBS or EMR number
- Departments — at least one is required, and they control who can see the encounter
- Care team — the staff who look after the patient, each with a clinical role, and one marked as primary
- Current location — the bed, room or ward the patient occupies
- Tags — labels the facility configures
- Hospitalization details — Re-admission, Admit Source, Discharge Disposition, Diet Preference. These appear only for Inpatient, Observation and Emergency encounters.
- Discharge Summary Advice — free text, available once the patient is discharged

### Status values (display labels)
Planned, In Progress, On Hold, Discharged, Completed, Cancelled, Discontinued, Entered in error, Unknown.
Terminal statuses that lock the encounter: Completed, Cancelled, Discontinued, Entered in error. Once an encounter reaches one of these, nobody can edit it or record new clinical data on it.

To close a discharged encounter, someone must still mark it as complete. State this plainly; it is the real behavior and the reader must know it.
Care applies no rules about which status can follow which. Any status can move to any other status while the encounter is still open.

### Type of Encounter values (display labels and meanings)
- Inpatient — Patient is admitted to the hospital
- Ambulatory — Patient visits for outpatient care
- Observation — Patient is under observation
- Emergency — Mark as emergency if immediate attention is required
- Virtual — Virtual/telehealth consultation
- Home Health — Care provided at patient's home

Stat, ASAP, Emergency, Urgent, Routine, Elective, Rush reporting, Timing critical, Callback results, Callback for scheduling, Pre-op, As needed, Use as directed. Routine is the default on the create form.

Home, Alternate home, Other health care facility, Hospice, Long term care, Left against advice, Expired, Psychiatric hospital, Rehabilitation, Skilled nursing facility, Other.

Vegetarian, Dairy free, Nut free, Gluten free, Vegan, Halal, Kosher, None.

### The location sheet
The sheet has two tabs: **Assign** and **History**.

**Assign a location**
1. Browse the facility's locations and select the bed or room the patient occupies. You can only assign a real place, such as a bed or a room. You cannot assign a location category.
2. Set the state of the stay. A stay can be planned, reserved or active. Only one stay can be active at a time.
3. Set the start time, and the end time when the stay has one.
4. Confirm.

**Move the patient to another location**
1. Select the new bed or room and choose the move action.
2. Care asks whether to keep the previous bed reserved for the patient, or to free it. Choose one.
3. Confirm.

**When the bed is taken**
- If an open encounter already occupies the bed, Care blocks the assignment and tells you the bed is occupied. You cannot override this. Free that bed first.

The History tab lists the patient's earlier stays for this encounter. From it you can correct the times of a stay, close a stay, or cancel a stay. Care asks you to confirm before it removes a stay.

- The end time must be the same as or later than the start time. Otherwise Care shows "End Datetime should be greater than Start Datetime".

- After you close a stay, you cannot change its state again.
- Two stays cannot overlap at the same location. Care shows "Conflict in schedule".
- The location and the encounter must belong to the same facility.
- While a patient occupies a bed, Care shows the bed as reserved. When the stay closes, Care shows the bed as available again.
- When you set the encounter status to Completed, Cancelled, Discontinued or Entered in error, Care closes any open stay for you.
- A discharged encounter still holds its location. Care only frees the bed when the stay closes or when someone marks the encounter as complete.

Care groups locations as Site, Building, Wing, Ward, Level, Corridor, Room, Bed, Vehicle, House, Cabinet, Road, Area, Jurisdiction and Virtual.

### Who can do this
Permission "Update Encounter non clinical" — Administrator, Doctor, Nurse and Facility Administrator. You also need permission to see the facility's locations.

### Before you start
The encounter exists and is still open. The facility has locations set up, and the bed or room you want belongs to the same facility as the encounter.

### Entry points
- On the encounter page, open **Encounter Actions** (shortcut `Shift+E`) and select **Assign Location**.
- Or press `l` on the encounter page.
- Or, on the **Overview** tab side panel, select **Update Location**.

### The location sheet
The sheet has two tabs: **Assign** and **History**.

**Assign a location**
1. Browse the facility's locations and select the bed or room the patient occupies. You can only assign a real place, such as a bed or a room. You cannot assign a location category.
2. Set the state of the stay. A stay can be planned, reserved or active. Only one stay can be active at a time.
3. Set the start time, and the end time when the stay has one.
4. Confirm.

**Move the patient to another location**
1. Select the new bed or room and choose the move action.
2. Care asks whether to keep the previous bed reserved for the patient, or to free it. Choose one.
3. Confirm.

**When the bed is taken**
- If an open encounter already occupies the bed, Care blocks the assignment and tells you the bed is occupied. You cannot override this. Free that bed first.
- If the encounter that occupies the bed is discharged, Care asks you to confirm before it moves the new patient in.

**History tab**
The History tab lists the patient's earlier stays for this encounter. From it you can correct the times of a stay, close a stay, or cancel a stay. Care asks you to confirm before it removes a stay.

### Rules Care applies
- The end time must be the same as or later than the start time. Otherwise Care shows "End Datetime should be greater than Start Datetime".
- A closed stay needs an end time. Otherwise Care shows "End Datetime is required for completed status".
- After you close a stay, you cannot change its state again.
- Two stays cannot overlap at the same location. Care shows "Conflict in schedule".
- The location and the encounter must belong to the same facility.
- While a patient occupies a bed, Care shows the bed as reserved. When the stay closes, Care shows the bed as available again.
- When you set the encounter status to Completed, Cancelled, Discontinued or Entered in error, Care closes any open stay for you.
- A discharged encounter still holds its location. Care only frees the bed when the stay closes or when someone marks the encounter as complete.

### Vocabulary
Care groups locations as Site, Building, Wing, Ward, Level, Corridor, Room, Bed, Vehicle, House, Cabinet, Road, Area, Jurisdiction and Virtual.

### Note
A user who belongs to the department that owns the patient's current bed can open the encounter, even when that user does not belong to the encounter's own departments.

### Entry points
1. **From the patient page.** Open the patient at the facility and select the **Create Encounter** quick action. Keyboard shortcut: `e`.
2. **From the patient's Encounters tab.** Open the patient, go to the **Encounters** tab, and select **Create Encounter** when the patient has no encounter yet.
3. **From an appointment — Start Consultation.** On the appointment page, in **Quick Actions**, select **Start Consultation** (shortcut `1`). Care opens the same form with the status already set to **In Progress** and links the encounter to the appointment. When you confirm, Care also moves the appointment to In Consultation.

4. **From an appointment — Create Planned Encounter.** In the same Quick Actions panel, select **Create Planned Encounter** (shortcut `2`). Care opens the form with the status already set to **Planned**.

### The form
Title: **Initiate Patient Encounter**. Below it Care shows "Begin a new clinical encounter for" and the patient's name.

Steps and fields, in the order they appear:
1. **Date and Time** (required) — pick the date and enter the time the encounter starts. You can only pick a future date when the status is Planned.
2. **Type of Encounter** (required) — select one tile. The tiles show Inpatient, Ambulatory, Observation, Emergency, Virtual and Home Health with a short description each. Your deployment decides which tiles appear and which one Care preselects.
3. **Status** (required) — choose **In Progress**, **Planned** or **On Hold**. These are the only statuses you can set at creation.
4. **Priority** (required) — choose from Stat, ASAP, Emergency, Urgent, Routine, Elective, Rush reporting, Timing critical, Callback results, Callback for scheduling, Pre-op, As needed and Use as directed. Care preselects **Routine**.
5. **Tags** (optional) — select one or more tags your facility configured for encounters.
6. **Departments** (required) — select at least one department. Departments control who can see the encounter, so choose the teams that look after the patient.
7. Select **Create Encounter**. The button shows "Creating…" while Care saves. Select **Cancel** to close the form without saving.

### Result
Care shows "Encounter created successfully" and opens the new encounter on its Overview tab.

### Errors the user can meet
- "Future date is only allowed for planned encounters" — the start date is in the future but the status is not Planned. Either move the date back or set the status to Planned.
- "At least one department is required" — the Create Encounter button stays disabled until you select a department.
- "Patient already has maximum number of active encounters (5) in the facility" — the patient already has the maximum number of open encounters at this facility. Close one of them first, or continue in the existing encounter. Your deployment sets this maximum; 5 is the default.
- "Encounter already has an associated booking" — the appointment you started from already has an encounter. Open that encounter instead.

### Notes
- Which encounter types you can choose, and which one Care preselects, depend on your deployment's configuration.
- The maximum number of open encounters per patient at a facility depends on your deployment's configuration.

### Before you start
The encounter exists and is still open. Care refuses every change to an encounter that is Completed, Cancelled, Discontinued or Entered in error. A **Discharged** encounter is still open, so you can still update it.

### Entry points
- On the encounter page, open **Encounter Actions** (shortcut `Shift+E`) and select **Update Encounter Details**.
- Or press `Shift+U` on the encounter page to open the same form directly.

### The form
Care opens the encounter form. It has these fields:
1. **Encounter Status** (required) — the list holds Planned, In Progress, On Hold, Completed, Cancelled, Discontinued and Entered in error. Care leaves Discharged out of the list, because you set that status with the discharge button described below. Once the patient is discharged, Care disables this field.
2. **Encounter Class** (required) — Inpatient, Ambulatory, Observation, Emergency, Virtual or Home Health. Your deployment decides which of these appear.
3. **Priority** (required) — Stat, ASAP, Emergency, Urgent, Routine, Elective, Rush reporting, Timing critical, Callback results, Callback for scheduling, Pre-op, As needed or Use as directed.
4. **Hospital Identifier** (optional) — the facility's reference number for this encounter. The field shows the hint "IP/OP/OBS/EMR Number".
5. **Discharge Summary Advice** (optional) — a free-text box. Care shows it after the patient is discharged, or when the encounter already holds advice.
6. **Hospitalization Details** — Care shows this section only for Inpatient, Observation and Emergency encounters. It holds:
   - **Re-admission** — a switch. Turn it on when the patient comes back for the same problem.
   - **Admit Source** — Transferred from other hospital, From accident/emergency department, From outpatient department, Born in hospital, General Practitioner referral, Medical Practitioner/physician referral, From nursing home, From psychiatric hospital, From rehabilitation facility, or Other.
   - **Discharge Disposition** — Home, Alternate home, Other health care facility, Hospice, Long term care, Left against advice, Expired, Psychiatric hospital, Rehabilitation, Skilled nursing facility, or Other.
   - **Diet Preference** — Vegetarian, Dairy free, Nut free, Gluten free, Vegan, Halal, Kosher, or None.
7. Submit the form. Care saves the encounter through the standard form submission.

The form also holds a **Mark for discharge** button. It is covered in the Discharge a patient flow — cross-link to it rather than describing it here.

### Behavior to record
- Care keeps a history of every status change and every encounter class change on the encounter.
- Care applies no rules about which status can follow which. While the encounter is open, you can set any status.
- When you set a status of Completed, Cancelled, Discontinued or Entered in error, Care closes any open location stay for the encounter and releases any device linked to it. After that, nobody can edit the encounter.
- If you clear Discharge Summary Advice and save, Care removes the earlier text.

### Notes
- Which encounter classes you can choose depends on your deployment's configuration.

### Who can do this
Permission "Update Encounter non clinical" — Administrator, Doctor, Nurse and Facility Administrator.

### Before you start
The patient has an open encounter of the type Inpatient, Observation or Emergency, and the patient is ready to leave the facility.

### Entry points
- On the **Overview** tab side panel, select the bottom button **Mark for discharge**.
- Or open **Encounter Actions** (shortcut `Shift+E`) and select **Mark for discharge**. The keyboard shortcut is `m` then `c`.
- Or open the encounter form (shortcut `Shift+U`) and select **Discharge Patient**.

For an Inpatient encounter that is not discharged yet, Care does not show the completion dialog. Care opens the encounter form with the discharge already selected, so that you can fill in the discharge details.

### Steps
1. Start the discharge from one of the entry points above. Care sets the **Encounter Status** to **Discharged** and disables the field.
2. **Discharge Disposition** (required) — select where the patient goes. The choices are Home, Alternate home, Other health care facility, Hospice, Long term care, Left against advice, Expired, Psychiatric hospital, Rehabilitation, Skilled nursing facility and Other. Care marks this field with an asterisk and refuses the form until you fill it in, for Inpatient, Observation and Emergency encounters. Your deployment can pre-fill a default choice.
3. **Discharge Date and Time** — set when the patient leaves. Care shows this field once the status is Discharged. The time cannot be earlier than the start of the encounter.
4. **Discharge Summary Advice** (optional) — write the advice the patient takes home.
5. Check the rest of the **Hospitalization Details**, such as **Admit Source**, **Re-admission** and **Diet Preference**.
6. Submit the form.

### What happens after the discharge — read this carefully
Care marks the encounter as **Discharged**, but the encounter stays open. This is deliberate:
- The care team can still change the encounter, the location, the care team, the departments and the tags.
- The patient keeps the bed until someone closes the location stay. Care only frees the bed when the stay closes or when someone marks the encounter as complete.
- To close the encounter, someone must mark it as complete. See the Complete an Encounter flow.
- Care can move a discharged encounter to another status, because Care applies no rules about which status follows which.

### Note
Your deployment can set a default discharge disposition, and it decides which encounter types your facility uses.

## VERIFIED FACTS

### FHIR R5 alignment
Care's Encounter follows the FHIR R5 Encounter resource (https://build.fhir.org/encounter.html). Link it on first mention.
Care implements: status, class, priority, subject (the patient), the facility that provides the service, location, participant (as the care team), appointment, period (start and end), and the admission details (admit source, re-admission, diet preference, discharge disposition). Care records one encounter class at a time and keeps a history of every status change and class change on the encounter itself, instead of a separate FHIR EncounterHistory resource. Care stores a single free-text hospital identifier rather than the structured FHIR identifier. Care's Encounter has no diagnosis element.
Related resources an Encounter links to: Patient, Organization (the facility and its departments), Location (the bed or room), and Appointment (the booking the encounter started from).

### What an Encounter is, for the reader
An Encounter records one interaction between a patient and the facility — an outpatient visit, an admission, an observation stay, an emergency visit, a virtual consultation, or a home visit. It groups everything the care team records for that interaction. A patient can have several encounters at a facility at the same time; the deployment sets the maximum (5 unless the deployment changes it).

### Key attributes (use these user-facing labels)
- Status
- Type of Encounter (called Encounter Class on the update form)
- Priority
- Date and Time (the start), and Discharge Date and Time (the end)
- Hospital Identifier — a free-text reference number the facility uses, such as an IP, OP, OBS or EMR number
- Departments — at least one is required, and they control who can see the encounter
- Care team — the staff who look after the patient, each with a clinical role, and one marked as primary
- Current location — the bed, room or ward the patient occupies
- Tags — labels the facility configures
- Hospitalization details — Re-admission, Admit Source, Discharge Disposition, Diet Preference. These appear only for Inpatient, Observation and Emergency encounters.
- Discharge Summary Advice — free text, available once the patient is discharged

### Status values (display labels)
Planned, In Progress, On Hold, Discharged, Completed, Cancelled, Discontinued, Entered in error, Unknown.
Terminal statuses that lock the encounter: Completed, Cancelled, Discontinued, Entered in error. Once an encounter reaches one of these, nobody can edit it or record new clinical data on it.
IMPORTANT AND DELIBERATE: **Discharged is not a terminal status in Care.** A discharged encounter stays editable — the care team can still change the location, the care team, the departments and the tags. To close a discharged encounter, someone must still mark it as complete. State this plainly; it is the real behavior and the reader must know it.
Care applies no rules about which status can follow which. Any status can move to any other status while the encounter is still open.

### Type of Encounter values (display labels and meanings)
- Inpatient — Patient is admitted to the hospital
- Ambulatory — Patient visits for outpatient care
- Observation — Patient is under observation
- Emergency — Mark as emergency if immediate attention is required
- Virtual — Virtual/telehealth consultation
- Home Health — Care provided at patient's home
Note: the deployment decides which of these appear, and which one is preselected.

### Priority values (display labels)
Stat, ASAP, Emergency, Urgent, Routine, Elective, Rush reporting, Timing critical, Callback results, Callback for scheduling, Pre-op, As needed, Use as directed. Routine is the default on the create form.

### Admit Source values (display labels)
Transferred from other hospital, From accident/emergency department, From outpatient department, Born in hospital, General Practitioner referral, Medical Practitioner/physician referral, From nursing home, From psychiatric hospital, From rehabilitation facility, Other.

### Discharge Disposition values (display labels)
Home, Alternate home, Other health care facility, Hospice, Long term care, Left against advice, Expired, Psychiatric hospital, Rehabilitation, Skilled nursing facility, Other.

### Diet Preference values (display labels)
Vegetarian, Dairy free, Nut free, Gluten free, Vegan, Halal, Kosher, None.
(The product currently shows a misspelling for the Dairy free option; do not mention this in the doc — write "Dairy free".)

### Tag categories (display labels)
Diet, Drug, Lab, Admin, Contact, Clinical, Behavioral, Research, Advance Directive, Safety.

### Where an Encounter appears in the product
- The facility sidebar has a Patients group with Search Patients, All Encounters (only when the deployment allows more than one encounter type), one list per allowed encounter type, and Locations.
- The encounter page has an Encounter Actions command palette (open it with Shift+E) and these tabs: Overview, Plots, Observations, Medicines, Responses, Service Requests, Diagnostic Reports, Files, Notes, Devices, Consents. Every tab except Overview, Devices and Consents needs permission to read clinical data.
- The Overview tab carries a side panel with Manage Consents, Manage Care Team, Update Location, Update Department and Dispense, plus a button to mark the encounter for discharge or as completed.
- A left rail lets the user switch between the patient's encounters and filter them by status, department, care team, date and tags.

### Permissions (human-readable names) — held by Administrator, Doctor, Nurse and Facility Administrator
- "Can Create encounter" — create an encounter
- "Can Read encounter" — open an encounter
- "Can list encounters" — see the encounter lists
- "Update Encounter non clinical" — change the encounter's own details, and manage its departments, care team, location, tags, completion and restart
- "Can Read encounter related clinical data" — open the clinical tabs
- "Update Encounter related clinical data" — record clinical data
- "Can submit questionnaire about patient encounters" — also held by Staff
A user can also reach an encounter through the department that owns the patient's current bed, not only through the encounter's own departments.

### Deployment configuration that changes behavior
- Which encounter types staff can choose, and which one is preselected.
- A default discharge disposition that Care pre-fills.
- The maximum number of open encounters one patient can have at a facility (5 by default).
- How long after its last change a completed encounter can be restarted (zero hours by default, which stops restarts until the deployment raises it).
- The default date filter on the encounter lists.
