Permission "Update Encounter non clinical" — Administrator, Doctor, Nurse and Facility Administrator. You also need permission to see the facility's locations.

### Before you start
The encounter exists and is still open. The facility has locations set up, and the bed or room you want belongs to the same facility as the encounter.

### Entry points
- On the encounter page, open **Encounter Actions** (shortcut `Shift+E`) and select **Assign Location**.
- Or press `l` on the encounter page.
- Or, on the **Overview** tab side panel, select **Update Location**.

### The location sheet
The sheet has two tabs: **Assign** and **History**.

**Assign a location**
1. Browse the facility's locations and select the bed or room the patient occupies. You can only assign a real place, such as a bed or a room. You cannot assign a location category.
2. Set the state of the stay. A stay can be planned, reserved or active. Only one stay can be active at a time.
3. Set the start time, and the end time when the stay has one.
4. Confirm.

**Move the patient to another location**
1. Select the new bed or room and choose the move action.
2. Care asks whether to keep the previous bed reserved for the patient, or to free it. Choose one.
3. Confirm.

**When the bed is taken**
- If an open encounter already occupies the bed, Care blocks the assignment and tells you the bed is occupied. You cannot override this. Free that bed first.
- If the encounter that occupies the bed is discharged, Care asks you to confirm before it moves the new patient in.

**History tab**
The History tab lists the patient's earlier stays for this encounter. From it you can correct the times of a stay, close a stay, or cancel a stay. Care asks you to confirm before it removes a stay.

### Rules Care applies
- The end time must be the same as or later than the start time. Otherwise Care shows "End Datetime should be greater than Start Datetime".
- A closed stay needs an end time. Otherwise Care shows "End Datetime is required for completed status".
- After you close a stay, you cannot change its state again.
- Two stays cannot overlap at the same location. Care shows "Conflict in schedule".
- The location and the encounter must belong to the same facility.
- While a patient occupies a bed, Care shows the bed as reserved. When the stay closes, Care shows the bed as available again.
- When you set the encounter status to Completed, Cancelled, Discontinued or Entered in error, Care closes any open stay for you.
- A discharged encounter still holds its location. Care only frees the bed when the stay closes or when someone marks the encounter as complete.

### Vocabulary
Care groups locations as Site, Building, Wing, Ward, Level, Corridor, Room, Bed, Vehicle, House, Cabinet, Road, Area, Jurisdiction and Virtual.

### Note
A user who belongs to the department that owns the patient's current bed can open the encounter, even when that user does not belong to the encounter's own departments.

### Before you start
The patient is registered in Care and you have opened the patient at the facility. If you start from an appointment, the patient has a booked or checked-in appointment at that facility.

### Entry points
1. **From the patient page.** Open the patient at the facility and select the **Create Encounter** quick action. Keyboard shortcut: `e`.
2. **From the patient's Encounters tab.** Open the patient, go to the **Encounters** tab, and select **Create Encounter** when the patient has no encounter yet.
3. **From an appointment — Start Consultation.** On the appointment page, in **Quick Actions**, select **Start Consultation** (shortcut `1`). Care opens the same form with the status already set to **In Progress** and links the encounter to the appointment. When you confirm, Care also moves the appointment to In Consultation.
   - If the appointment already has an encounter, **Start Consultation** does not open the form. Care moves the appointment to In Consultation and opens the existing encounter on its Overview tab.
4. **From an appointment — Create Planned Encounter.** In the same Quick Actions panel, select **Create Planned Encounter** (shortcut `2`). Care opens the form with the status already set to **Planned**.

### The form
Title: **Initiate Patient Encounter**. Below it Care shows "Begin a new clinical encounter for" and the patient's name.

Steps and fields, in the order they appear:
1. **Date and Time** (required) — pick the date and enter the time the encounter starts. You can only pick a future date when the status is Planned.
2. **Type of Encounter** (required) — select one tile. The tiles show Inpatient, Ambulatory, Observation, Emergency, Virtual and Home Health with a short description each. Your deployment decides which tiles appear and which one Care preselects.
3. **Status** (required) — choose **In Progress**, **Planned** or **On Hold**. These are the only statuses you can set at creation.
4. **Priority** (required) — choose from Stat, ASAP, Emergency, Urgent, Routine, Elective, Rush reporting, Timing critical, Callback results, Callback for scheduling, Pre-op, As needed and Use as directed. Care preselects **Routine**.
5. **Tags** (optional) — select one or more tags your facility configured for encounters.
6. **Departments** (required) — select at least one department. Departments control who can see the encounter, so choose the teams that look after the patient.
7. Select **Create Encounter**. The button shows "Creating…" while Care saves. Select **Cancel** to close the form without saving.

### Result
Care shows "Encounter created successfully" and opens the new encounter on its Overview tab.

### Errors the user can meet
- "Future date is only allowed for planned encounters" — the start date is in the future but the status is not Planned. Either move the date back or set the status to Planned.
- "At least one department is required" — the Create Encounter button stays disabled until you select a department.
- "Patient already has maximum number of active encounters (5) in the facility" — the patient already has the maximum number of open encounters at this facility. Close one of them first, or continue in the existing encounter. Your deployment sets this maximum; 5 is the default.
- "Encounter already has an associated booking" — the appointment you started from already has an encounter. Open that encounter instead.

### Notes
- Which encounter types you can choose, and which one Care preselects, depend on your deployment's configuration.
- The maximum number of open encounters per patient at a facility depends on your deployment's configuration.

The encounter exists and is still open. Care refuses every change to an encounter that is Completed, Cancelled, Discontinued or Entered in error. A **Discharged** encounter is still open, so you can still update it.

- On the encounter page, open **Encounter Actions** (shortcut `Shift+E`) and select **Update Encounter Details**.

### The form
Care opens the encounter form. It has these fields:
1. **Encounter Status** (required) — the list holds Planned, In Progress, On Hold, Completed, Cancelled, Discontinued and Entered in error. Care leaves Discharged out of the list, because you set that status with the discharge button described below. Once the patient is discharged, Care disables this field.
2. **Encounter Class** (required) — Inpatient, Ambulatory, Observation, Emergency, Virtual or Home Health. Your deployment decides which of these appear.
3. **Priority** (required) — Stat, ASAP, Emergency, Urgent, Routine, Elective, Rush reporting, Timing critical, Callback results, Callback for scheduling, Pre-op, As needed or Use as directed.
4. **Hospital Identifier** (optional) — the facility's reference number for this encounter. The field shows the hint "IP/OP/OBS/EMR Number".
5. **Discharge Summary Advice** (optional) — a free-text box. Care shows it after the patient is discharged, or when the encounter already holds advice.
6. **Hospitalization Details** — Care shows this section only for Inpatient, Observation and Emergency encounters. It holds:
   - **Re-admission** — a switch. Turn it on when the patient comes back for the same problem.
   - **Admit Source** — Transferred from other hospital, From accident/emergency department, From outpatient department, Born in hospital, General Practitioner referral, Medical Practitioner/physician referral, From nursing home, From psychiatric hospital, From rehabilitation facility, or Other.
   - **Discharge Disposition** — Home, Alternate home, Other health care facility, Hospice, Long term care, Left against advice, Expired, Psychiatric hospital, Rehabilitation, Skilled nursing facility, or Other.
   - **Diet Preference** — Vegetarian, Dairy free, Nut free, Gluten free, Vegan, Halal, Kosher, or None.
7. Submit the form. Care saves the encounter through the standard form submission.

The form also holds a **Mark for discharge** button. It is covered in the Discharge a patient flow — cross-link to it rather than describing it here.

### Behavior to record
- Care keeps a history of every status change and every encounter class change on the encounter.
- Care applies no rules about which status can follow which. While the encounter is open, you can set any status.
- When you set a status of Completed, Cancelled, Discontinued or Entered in error, Care closes any open location stay for the encounter and releases any device linked to it. After that, nobody can edit the encounter.
- If you clear Discharge Summary Advice and save, Care removes the earlier text.

### Notes
- Which encounter classes you can choose depends on your deployment's configuration.

### Who can do this
Permission "Update Encounter non clinical" — Administrator, Doctor, Nurse and Facility Administrator.

### Before you start
The patient has an open encounter of the type Inpatient, Observation or Emergency, and the patient is ready to leave the facility.

### Entry points
- On the **Overview** tab side panel, select the bottom button **Mark for discharge**.
- Or open **Encounter Actions** (shortcut `Shift+E`) and select **Mark for discharge**. The keyboard shortcut is `m` then `c`.
- Or open the encounter form (shortcut `Shift+U`) and select **Discharge Patient**.

For an Inpatient encounter that is not discharged yet, Care does not show the completion dialog. Care opens the encounter form with the discharge already selected, so that you can fill in the discharge details.

### Steps
1. Start the discharge from one of the entry points above. Care sets the **Encounter Status** to **Discharged** and disables the field.
2. **Discharge Disposition** (required) — select where the patient goes. The choices are Home, Alternate home, Other health care facility, Hospice, Long term care, Left against advice, Expired, Psychiatric hospital, Rehabilitation, Skilled nursing facility and Other. Care marks this field with an asterisk and refuses the form until you fill it in, for Inpatient, Observation and Emergency encounters. Your deployment can pre-fill a default choice.
3. **Discharge Date and Time** — set when the patient leaves. Care shows this field once the status is Discharged. The time cannot be earlier than the start of the encounter.
4. **Discharge Summary Advice** (optional) — write the advice the patient takes home.
5. Check the rest of the **Hospitalization Details**, such as **Admit Source**, **Re-admission** and **Diet Preference**.
6. Submit the form.

### What happens after the discharge — read this carefully
Care marks the encounter as **Discharged**, but the encounter stays open. This is deliberate:
- The care team can still change the encounter, the location, the care team, the departments and the tags.
- The patient keeps the bed until someone closes the location stay. Care only frees the bed when the stay closes or when someone marks the encounter as complete.
- To close the encounter, someone must mark it as complete. See the Complete an Encounter flow.
- Care can move a discharged encounter to another status, because Care applies no rules about which status follows which.

### Note
Your deployment can set a default discharge disposition, and it decides which encounter types your facility uses.

## VERIFIED FACTS

### FHIR R5 alignment
Care's Encounter follows the FHIR R5 Encounter resource (https://build.fhir.org/encounter.html). Link it on first mention.
Care implements: status, class, priority, subject (the patient), the facility that provides the service, location, participant (as the care team), appointment, period (start and end), and the admission details (admit source, re-admission, diet preference, discharge disposition). Care records one encounter class at a time and keeps a history of every status change and class change on the encounter itself, instead of a separate FHIR EncounterHistory resource. Care stores a single free-text hospital identifier rather than the structured FHIR identifier. Care's Encounter has no diagnosis element.
Related resources an Encounter links to: Patient, Organization (the facility and its departments), Location (the bed or room), and Appointment (the booking the encounter started from).

### What an Encounter is, for the reader
An Encounter records one interaction between a patient and the facility — an outpatient visit, an admission, an observation stay, an emergency visit, a virtual consultation, or a home visit. It groups everything the care team records for that interaction. A patient can have several encounters at a facility at the same time; the deployment sets the maximum (5 unless the deployment changes it).

### Key attributes (use these user-facing labels)
- Status
- Type of Encounter (called Encounter Class on the update form)
- Priority
- Date and Time (the start), and Discharge Date and Time (the end)
- Hospital Identifier — a free-text reference number the facility uses, such as an IP, OP, OBS or EMR number
- Departments — at least one is required, and they control who can see the encounter
- Care team — the staff who look after the patient, each with a clinical role, and one marked as primary
- Current location — the bed, room or ward the patient occupies
- Tags — labels the facility configures
- Hospitalization details — Re-admission, Admit Source, Discharge Disposition, Diet Preference. These appear only for Inpatient, Observation and Emergency encounters.
- Discharge Summary Advice — free text, available once the patient is discharged

### Status values (display labels)
Planned, In Progress, On Hold, Discharged, Completed, Cancelled, Discontinued, Entered in error, Unknown.
Terminal statuses that lock the encounter: Completed, Cancelled, Discontinued, Entered in error. Once an encounter reaches one of these, nobody can edit it or record new clinical data on it.
IMPORTANT AND DELIBERATE: **Discharged is not a terminal status in Care.** A discharged encounter stays editable — the care team can still change the location, the care team, the departments and the tags. To close a discharged encounter, someone must still mark it as complete. State this plainly; it is the real behavior and the reader must know it.
Care applies no rules about which status can follow which. Any status can move to any other status while the encounter is still open.

### Type of Encounter values (display labels and meanings)
- Inpatient — Patient is admitted to the hospital
- Ambulatory — Patient visits for outpatient care
- Observation — Patient is under observation
- Emergency — Mark as emergency if immediate attention is required
- Virtual — Virtual/telehealth consultation
- Home Health — Care provided at patient's home
Note: the deployment decides which of these appear, and which one is preselected.

### Priority values (display labels)
Stat, ASAP, Emergency, Urgent, Routine, Elective, Rush reporting, Timing critical, Callback results, Callback for scheduling, Pre-op, As needed, Use as directed. Routine is the default on the create form.

### Admit Source values (display labels)
Transferred from other hospital, From accident/emergency department, From outpatient department, Born in hospital, General Practitioner referral, Medical Practitioner/physician referral, From nursing home, From psychiatric hospital, From rehabilitation facility, Other.

### Discharge Disposition values (display labels)
Home, Alternate home, Other health care facility, Hospice, Long term care, Left against advice, Expired, Psychiatric hospital, Rehabilitation, Skilled nursing facility, Other.

### Diet Preference values (display labels)
Vegetarian, Dairy free, Nut free, Gluten free, Vegan, Halal, Kosher, None.
(The product currently shows a misspelling for the Dairy free option; do not mention this in the doc — write "Dairy free".)

### Tag categories (display labels)
Diet, Drug, Lab, Admin, Contact, Clinical, Behavioral, Research, Advance Directive, Safety.

### Where an Encounter appears in the product
- The facility sidebar has a Patients group with Search Patients, All Encounters (only when the deployment allows more than one encounter type), one list per allowed encounter type, and Locations.
- The encounter page has an Encounter Actions command palette (open it with Shift+E) and these tabs: Overview, Plots, Observations, Medicines, Responses, Service Requests, Diagnostic Reports, Files, Notes, Devices, Consents. Every tab except Overview, Devices and Consents needs permission to read clinical data.
- The Overview tab carries a side panel with Manage Consents, Manage Care Team, Update Location, Update Department and Dispense, plus a button to mark the encounter for discharge or as completed.
- A left rail lets the user switch between the patient's encounters and filter them by status, department, care team, date and tags.

### Permissions (human-readable names) — held by Administrator, Doctor, Nurse and Facility Administrator
- "Can Create encounter" — create an encounter
- "Can Read encounter" — open an encounter
- "Can list encounters" — see the encounter lists
- "Update Encounter non clinical" — change the encounter's own details, and manage its departments, care team, location, tags, completion and restart
- "Can Read encounter related clinical data" — open the clinical tabs
- "Update Encounter related clinical data" — record clinical data
- "Can submit questionnaire about patient encounters" — also held by Staff
A user can also reach an encounter through the department that owns the patient's current bed, not only through the encounter's own departments.

### Deployment configuration that changes behavior
- Which encounter types staff can choose, and which one is preselected.
- A default discharge disposition that Care pre-fills.
- The maximum number of open encounters one patient can have at a facility (5 by default).
- How long after its last change a completed encounter can be restarted (zero hours by default, which stops restarts until the deployment raises it).
- The default date filter on the encounter lists.

Clinical - Encounter

## Definition An **[encounter](https://build.fhir.org/encounter.html)** in Care records one interaction between a patient and your facility. The interaction is an outpatient visit, an admission, an observation stay, an emergency visit, a virtual consultation, or a home visit. The encounter groups everything the care team records for that interaction. A patient can have more than one open encounter at the same facility at the same time. Note: Your deployment sets the maximum number of open encounters for one patient at a facility. The default maximum is 5. Care follows the FHIR R5 Encounter resource. An encounter links to the patient, to the facility and the departments that answer for the care, to the location that the patient occupies, and to the appointment that starts the encounter. ## Key Attributes | Components | What it captures | | --- | --- | | Status | The current state of the encounter, for example In Progress. | | Type of Encounter | The type of care, for example Inpatient or Ambulatory. The update form calls this field Encounter Class. | | Priority | The urgency of the care, for example Emergency or Routine. | | Date and Time | The date and time when the encounter starts. | | Discharge Date and Time | The date and time when the facility discharges the patient. | | Hospital Identifier | A free-text reference number that your facility uses, such as an IP, OP, OBS or EMR number. | | Departments | The facility departments that answer for the encounter. | | Care team | The staff who look after the patient, each with a clinical role. | | Current location | The bed, room or ward that the patient occupies. | | Tags | Labels that your facility configures. | | Hospitalization details | The admission and discharge information for a patient who stays at the facility. | | Discharge Summary Advice | Free text that the team writes for the patient at discharge. | ### Departments Each encounter needs at least one department. The departments control who can see the encounter. To change them, see [Manage Encounter departments](./flows/5.%20Manage%20Encounter%20departments.md). ### Care team The care team lists the staff who look after the patient. Each member holds a clinical role. One member carries the primary marker. To change the team, see [Manage the Encounter care team](./flows/4.%20Manage%20the%20Encounter%20care%20team.md). ### Tags Your facility configures the tags. Care groups them in these categories: - Diet - Drug - Lab - Admin - Contact - Clinical - Behavioral - Research - Advance Directive - Safety ### Type of Encounter | Type of Encounter | Description | | --- | --- | | Inpatient | Patient is admitted to the hospital. | | Ambulatory | Patient visits for outpatient care. | | Observation | Patient is under observation. | | Emergency | Mark as emergency if immediate attention is required. | | Virtual | Virtual/telehealth consultation. | | Home Health | Care provided at patient's home. | Note: Your deployment decides which types staff can choose. Your deployment also decides which type Care preselects. ### Priority The priority states how urgent the care is. Care offers these priorities: - Stat - ASAP - Emergency - Urgent - Routine - Elective - Rush reporting - Timing critical - Callback results - Callback for scheduling - Pre-op - As needed - Use as directed Note: Routine is the default priority on the create form. ### Hospitalization details Hospitalization details appear only for the Inpatient, Observation and Emergency types. | Components | What it captures | | --- | --- | | Re-admission | Whether the patient returns to the facility for the same problem. | | Admit Source | Where the patient comes from. | | Discharge Disposition | Where the patient goes after discharge. | | Diet Preference | The food requirement of the patient. | Admit Source offers these values: - Transferred from other hospital - From accident/emergency department - From outpatient department - Born in hospital - General Practitioner referral - Medical Practitioner/physician referral - From nursing home - From psychiatric hospital - From rehabilitation facility - Other Discharge Disposition offers these values: - Home - Alternate home - Other health care facility - Hospice - Long term care - Left against advice - Expired - Psychiatric hospital - Rehabilitation - Skilled nursing facility - Other Diet Preference offers these values: - Vegetarian - Dairy free - Nut free - Gluten free - Vegan - Halal - Kosher - None Note: Your deployment can set a default discharge disposition. Care pre-fills that value. ### Status The status shows where the encounter is in its life cycle. | Status | Description | | --- | --- | | Planned | The team plans the encounter for a future date. | | In Progress | The team gives care to the patient now. | | On Hold | The team pauses the encounter. | | Discharged | The facility discharges the patient. | | Completed | The care in this encounter ends. | | Cancelled | The team cancels the encounter before the care starts. | | Discontinued | The team stops the encounter before the care ends. | | Entered in error | A user creates the encounter by mistake. | | Unknown | The status of the encounter is not known. | Care applies no rules about the order of the statuses. While the encounter stays open, you can move it from any status to any other status. Four statuses lock the encounter: Completed, Cancelled, Discontinued and Entered in error. After the encounter reaches one of these statuses, nobody can edit it. Nobody can record new clinical data on it. Discharged does not lock the encounter. A discharged encounter stays open for edits. The care team can still change the location, the care team, the departments and the tags. To close a discharged encounter, someone must mark it as complete. See [Complete an Encounter](./flows/8.%20Complete%20an%20Encounter.md). Note: Your deployment sets how long after its last change someone can restart a completed encounter. The default is zero hours, which stops all restarts. ## Where to find Encounters The facility sidebar holds a Patients group. The group contains Search Patients, one list for each allowed encounter type, and Locations. The group also contains All Encounters when your deployment allows more than one encounter type. Note: Your deployment sets the default date filter on the encounter lists. The encounter page holds these tabs: Overview, Plots, Observations, Medicines, Responses, Service Requests, Diagnostic Reports, Files, Notes, Devices and Consents. Every tab except Overview, Devices and Consents needs permission to read clinical data. The encounter page also holds an Encounter Actions command palette. Press Shift+E to open it. The Overview tab carries a side panel with these actions: - Manage Consents - Manage Care Team - Update Location - Update Department - Dispense The Overview tab also carries a button that marks the encounter for discharge or as completed. A left rail lets you move between the encounters of the patient. The rail filters the encounters by status, department, care team, date and tags. ## Permissions Your role controls what you can do with an encounter. Administrators, Doctors, Nurses and Facility Administrators hold these permissions. | Permission | What it allows | | --- | --- | | Can Create encounter | Create an encounter. | | Can Read encounter | Open an encounter. | | Can list encounters | See the encounter lists. | | Update Encounter non clinical | Change the details of the encounter. Manage its departments, care team, location, tags, completion and restart. | | Can Read encounter related clinical data | Open the clinical tabs. | | Update Encounter related clinical data | Record clinical data. | | Can submit questionnaire about patient encounters | Answer questionnaires about the encounter. Staff also hold this permission. | You can also reach an encounter through the department that owns the current bed of the patient. The departments of the encounter are not the only route. ## Related - Flow: [Create an Encounter](./flows/1.%20Create%20an%20Encounter.md) - Flow: [Update Encounter details](./flows/2.%20Update%20Encounter%20details.md) - Flow: [Assign an Encounter location](./flows/3.%20Assign%20an%20Encounter%20location.md) - Flow: [Manage the Encounter care team](./flows/4.%20Manage%20the%20Encounter%20care%20team.md) - Flow: [Manage Encounter departments](./flows/5.%20Manage%20Encounter%20departments.md) - Flow: [Manage Encounter tags](./flows/6.%20Manage%20Encounter%20tags.md) - Flow: [Discharge a patient](./flows/7.%20Discharge%20a%20patient.md) - Flow: [Complete an Encounter](./flows/8.%20Complete%20an%20Encounter.md) - Flow: [Restart an Encounter](./flows/9.%20Restart%20an%20Encounter.md)

replacements.newString:
1. Select the department the person belongs to.
2. Open **Select Member** and choose the person. Care lists only the users of the department you chose.
3. Open **Select Role** and choose the clinical role of the person. Care shows the roles that match your search.
4. Select **Add**. Care shows "Member added successfully".

Note: The list of roles comes from a clinical terminology set. Your deployment can offer a different set of roles from another deployment.

If you select a person who is already on the team, Care shows "Member already added".

### 3. Set the primary member

Select **Mark as Primary** on a member. Care moves that person to the top of the list. Care shows "Primary member updated". Care asks for no confirmation.

Note: Care keeps the first person in the list as the primary member. Care marks that person **Primary**.

### 4. Remove a member

Select **Remove** on the member. Care opens the **Confirm Removing Member** dialog. Select **Remove** again. Care shows "Member removed successfully".

If you select a person who is already on the team, Care shows "Member already added".

### 3. Set the primary member

Select **Make Primary** on a member. Care moves that person to the top of the list. Care shows "Primary member updated". Care asks for no confirmation.

Note: Care keeps the first person in the list as the primary member.

### 4. Remove a member

Select the remove action on the member. Confirm in the dialog. Care shows "Member removed successfully".

## Changes by file

**concept.md**

- Verified: FHIR R5 link `https://build.fhir.org/encounter.html` present on first mention; centered H1; Discharged correctly described as non-terminal.

**1. Create an Encounter.md**
- Added the verified Type of Encounter tile-description table (Inpatient, Ambulatory, Observation, Emergency, Virtual, Home Health).
- Replaced the 30-word Priority enumeration with a pointer to the concept doc.
- Added the missing Related links to flows 7, 8 and 9.

**2. Update Encounter details.md**
- Pre-requisite rewritten from data-model phrasing ("The encounter exists in Care") to the user's situation.
- Shortened three over-length enumeration sentences (Priority, Admit Source, Discharge Disposition, Diet Preference) by pointing to the concept doc.
- `Re-admission` → `Re-Admission`; "The food the patient takes" → "The dietary requirement of the patient".
- Added a note that the create form calls **Encounter Class** **Type of Encounter** (resolves the cross-doc label mismatch).
- Left the submit button label and post-save confirmation generic, as instructed.

**3. Assign an Encounter location.md**
- Pre-requisite rewritten to the user's situation.
- "A stay can be planned…" → "A stay is planned…" (removed the `can be` construction).
- Broke the 22-word location-form list into bullets.
- Rewrote two data-model sentences: an encounter no longer "occupies" a bed — the patient does.
- Left the move action, keep-reserved choice and History tab actions generic, as instructed.

**4. Manage the Encounter care team.md**
- H1 → "How to Manage the Encounter **Care Team**" (Title Case, consistent with the other eight).
- Pre-requisite rewritten to the user's situation.
- **Corrected an unverified label**: "Make Primary" → **Mark as Primary**. The former does not exist.
- Filled in the add-member form labels from the frontend source rather than leaving them vague: **Select Member**, **Select Role**, **Add**, **Remove**, **Confirm Removing Member**, and the **Primary** marker. You asked me not to invent these — I did not; I read them out of the care team sheet component and the English locale file.

**5 / 6. Manage Encounter departments / tags.md**
- H1s → "…**Departments**" / "…**Tags**" (Title Case).
- Pre-requisites rewritten to the user's situation.

**7. Discharge a patient.md**
- Applied all three verified values: **Admit Source** ("Where the patient came from") with its ten choices as a list; **Re-Admission** described as a switch you turn on when the patient comes back for the same problem; **Diet Preference** ("The dietary requirement of the patient") with its eight choices as a list.

**8. Complete an Encounter.md**
- Dialog title corrected to **Mark as Complete** (title case), and the confirm button named explicitly.
- "If the patient was admitted" → "If the facility admits the patient" (present tense, active voice).

**9. Restart an Encounter.md** — no violations found; unchanged.

## Verification notes

- Cross-links: all links in the ten files resolve to one of the ten files or `../concept.md`, all use `%20`. No links to the ten obsolete snake_case files, which I did not open or touch.
- Discharge is consistently non-terminal across the concept doc and flows 2, 3, 7 and 8. Nothing implies discharge closes an encounter.
- Terminology: labels cross-checked against `care_fe/public/locale/en.json`.
